method: Individual comparison against available original museum catalogues, scholarly collection pages, historic artwork identity, and intended saint/feast; uncertain secondary records explicitly held; pixel, license, crop and owner changes not cleared

high_priority_differences: Le Brun Bruges work is a copy after Edelinck, not autograph Le Brun
Bourdon work is a reduced version with revised St Martin vs St Gregory title
Prado Coello object intrinsically relevant but disallowed photographic source
Zurbarán Agatha proposal link is a detail crop rather than complete artwork
Elizabeth/Pierre catalogue attribution and Vaccaro inventory remain unverified

records.claude_claim: Zurbarán's Saint Agatha depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée Fabre, Montpellier inv. 852.1.3, Zurbarán, circa 1635–1640; depicted St Agatha with breasts on a plate
records.findings: The Musée Fabre official catalogue confirms the saint and original object. Claude's specified Commons link is a cropped 'detalle' PNG, not an independently cleared reproduction of the complete canvas.

records.observance: Vigil of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist
records.artwork_title: Johannes Moreelse, Saint John the Baptist
records.claude_claim: Moreelse's St John the Baptist portrait for the Vigil. The Zechariah scene (Luke 1:5–17) exists only as an unapproved legacy work.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon, reportedly A 2853, Johannes Moreelse; 1630s oil on canvas; Lyon object included in Musée des Augustins 2012 institution exhibition list
records.findings: The picture is of adult St John the Baptist. For June 23 vigil the Gospel is Luke 1:5–17 and concerns Zacharias; this portrait is appropriate saint iconography, not a representation of the announced conception. Direct Lyon catalogue/inventory image matching is not yet independently completed.

records.artwork_title: Domenico Antonio Vaccaro, Mystical Vision of Saint Bonaventure
records.claude_claim: Vaccaro's Vision of St Bonaventure (legacy approved) depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Museo dell'Opera di San Lorenzo Maggiore, Naples; formerly second chapel on right dedicated to Bonaventure; Domenico Antonio Vaccaro, oil on canvas about 200×240cm per ARTE.it guide
records.findings: The named vision depicts the saint of the feast. The current Claude record says artist attribution not established; a secondary Italian cultural guide identifies Vaccaro. Do not promote the photographer's Commons credit into creator, or treat the secondary guide as a verified institutional accession and attribution.

records.claude_claim: Reni's Saint Mary Magdalene (legacy approved) depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Walters Art Museum Baltimore 37.2631, Guido Reni, ca.1635, oil on canvas, 90.8×74.3cm
records.findings: The exact uploaded Google Art Project file references Walters 37.2631. Walters confirms attribution and Magdalene iconography; many Reni and workshop versions exist, including separate London NG177 and Crespi after Reni Walters 37.1130. The painting does not literally depict the July 22 appointed Gospel or identify its Magdalene figure.

records.artwork_title: Claudio Coello, Saint Dominic of Guzmán
records.claude_claim: Coello's Saint Dominic of Guzmán (legacy approved).
records.physical_work_identity: Museo del Prado P000662, Claudio Coello ca.1685, oil on canvas 240×160cm, originally Madrid Dominican convent El Rosario
records.findings: The institutional catalogue confirms exact artist and saint, but the painting is Prado owned and the user's Prado photographic-source exclusion remains binding. Preserve earlier artwork selection historically; neither new Prado photo nor automatic display is authorised.

records.artwork_title: Adam Elsheimer, Saint Lawrence Prepared for Martyrdom
records.claude_claim: Elsheimer's Saint Lawrence depicts the martyr of the feast.
records.physical_work_identity: National Gallery London NG1014, Elsheimer ca.1601–02, oil on copper 26.7×20.6cm
records.findings: National Gallery confirms the work as autograph Elsheimer; it shows Lawrence being prepared for martyrdom, not the actual death or Gospel. Gallery scholarly catalogue documents several different copies/versions; retain exact NG1014 identity.

records.observance: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
records.artwork_title: Greek school, The Birth of the Virgin
records.claude_claim: The Greek-school icon of the Birth of the Virgin depicts the feast (a tradition, not a canonical Gospel scene).
records.physical_work_identity: Petit Palais Paris Musées PPP4898; Greek-school icon, signed 'Johannis' 1785, tempera on wood, 54.7×36.3cm
records.findings: Paris Musées identifies the birth of Mary, with Anne, Joachim and child. This is a noncanonical Marian tradition, suitable to Nativity of the Blessed Virgin. The museum page labels digital media CC0, but the specific Commons file, crop and mobile image QA remain unreviewed.

records.artwork_title: Christ on the Cross Surrounded by Angels, after Le Brun
records.claude_claim: Le Brun's Christ on the Cross surrounded by angels for the Exaltation of the Cross; Rubens's Brazen Serpent is the typological alternative (John 3:14).
records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge 0000.GRO0470.I, 17th-century oil on canvas 116×90.5cm; original maker unnamed, composition copied after Gerard Edelinck engraving derived from Charles Le Brun
records.findings: Bruges explicitly states the painting is copied from Edelinck's print after Le Brun's composition. Claude's credit 'Charles Le Brun' as painting creator is false for this specific physical object. The work is relevant to Exaltation but not the biblical Bronze Serpent reading (John 3:13–17) literally.

records.artwork_title: Corrado Giaquinto, Saint Margaret Mary Contemplating the Sacred Heart
records.claude_claim: Giaquinto's St Margaret Mary Contemplating the Sacred Heart depicts the saint (research proposal). The WGA reproduction is low resolution.
records.physical_work_identity: Private collection, Giaquinto ca.1765, oil on canvas, 171×123cm per Web Gallery of Art
records.findings: Identifies Margaret Mary Alacoque contemplating Sacred Heart. No public institution accession; WGA/Commons is 750×1040 low-res, not cleared against original photo or publication requirements. Valid saint-devotion thematic relationship, not appointed Gospel narrative.

records.artwork_title: Eustache Le Sueur, Archangel Raphael Reveals His Identity to Tobias and Family
records.claude_claim: Le Sueur's Angel taking leave of Tobias depicts the archangel Raphael. The van der Neer Tobias stays quarantined.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée de Grenoble, Eustache Le Sueur 1647, oil on canvas 173×215cm, original ceiling panel of Hôtel de Fieubet
records.findings: Grenoble museum explicitly identifies Raphael's revelation following the cure of Tobit's blindness (Tobit 12), at the moment the angel ascends. Correct Raphael feast association, not the day Gospel and not simply generic angel departing.

records.artwork_title: Sébastien Bourdon, Miracle of Saint Martin
records.claude_claim: Bourdon's Miracle of St Martin depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée national Magnin Dijon 1938 F 97, Bourdon, oil on canvas 52.5×40cm; reduced version of destroyed original commissioned for Cologne Cathedral
records.findings: The French museum catalogue explicitly revises previous 'Miracle of St Gregory Thaumaturgus' identification to St Martin's miracle of resurrection, citing historical manuscript. This object is a reduced replica/version, not the destroyed Cologne painting. Official photograph RMN permission-restricted.

records.artwork_title: Murillo, Saint Didacus of Alcalá in Ecstasy Before the Cross
records.claude_claim: Murillo's San Diego (Didacus) in ecstasy before the cross depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Louvre owned D 1846 1 / RO 415, Murillo 1645–46, on long-term loan Musée des Augustins Toulouse, 173×186cm
records.findings: Louvre catalogue confirms the depicted Didacus (Diego) of Alcalá and current loan. Claude's Commons image is only 800×746 and credited to local museum photothèque; an alternative photo exists but its independent source/reuse and crop must be reviewed.

records.observance: Dedication of the Basilicas of Sts. Peter & Paul
records.artwork_title: Jusepe de Ribera, Saints Peter and Paul
records.claude_claim: Ribera's Saints Peter and Paul for the dedication of their basilicas.
records.physical_work_identity: Musées de Strasbourg MBA 180, Ribera ca.1616, oil on canvas, 126×112cm; Zeri flags historical alternative Gérard Douffet attribution
records.findings: The physical painting is institutional record MBA180 and depicts Peter and Paul, patrons of the two basilicas whose dedication is observed. It does NOT depict either basilica building or consecration ritual. Strasbourg museum instructs users to contact photothèque for image re-use; do not newly publish.

records.artwork_title: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, attributed to Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre
records.claude_claim: Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre's Saint Elizabeth of Hungary depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée national Magnin Dijon inventory 1938 F 651, Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, credited Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre in Commons and derivatives; POP notice 50110000916 indexed but full entry not independently retrieved
records.findings: Matches the saint of the day by title, but official catalogue detail and current painter attribution have not been independently verified. Keep Claude's '(attrib.)' and exact digital image under explicit hold; do not certify the saint's exact story or painter autograph.

records.artwork_title: Gaspar de Crayer, Martyrdom of Saint Catherine
records.claude_claim: De Crayer's Martyrdom of St Catherine depicts the saint of the day.
records.physical_work_identity: Musée de Grenoble, de Crayer ca.1622, oil on canvas 242×188cm, state deposit since 1799
records.findings: Grenoble curator identifies Saint Catherine of Alexandria, represented immediately before her beheading after the wheel ordeal, following Golden Legend account. Feast subject is exact hagiography, not a canonical Gospel scene. Grenoble photo credited J.-L. Lacroix separately from historic public domain work.
